author: Thomas à Kempis
title: That man hath no good in himself, and nothing whereof to glory

notes.text: (1) Psalm viii. 4. (2) 2 Corinthians xii. 5. (3) John v. 44.

verses.text: Lord, what is man that Thou art mindful of him, or the son of man that Thou visitest him?(1) What hath man deserved, that Thou shouldest bestow thy favour upon him?
verses.modernizedText: Lord, what is man that You are mindful of him, or the son of man that You visit him?(1) What has man deserved, that You should bestow Your favor upon him?

verses.text: Lord, what cause can I have of complaint, if Thou forsake me?
verses.modernizedText: Lord, what cause can I have for complaint if You forsake me?

verses.text: Or what can I justly allege, if Thou refuse to hear my petition?
verses.modernizedText: Or what can I justly allege if You refuse to hear my petition?

verses.text: Of a truth, this I may truly think and say, Lord, I am nothing, I have nothing that is good of myself, but I fall short in all things, and ever tend unto nothing.
verses.modernizedText: In truth, this I may truly think and say: Lord, I am nothing, I have nothing that is good of myself, but I fall short in all things, and ever tend toward nothing.

verses.text: And unless I am helped by Thee and inwardly supported, I become altogether lukewarm and reckless.
verses.modernizedText: And unless I am helped by You and inwardly supported, I become altogether lukewarm and reckless.

verses.text: But Thou, O Lord, art always the same, and endurest for ever, always good, righteous, and holy; doing all things well, righteously, and holily, and disposing all in Thy wisdom.
verses.modernizedText: But You, O Lord, are always the same, and endure forever, always good, righteous, and holy; doing all things well, righteously, and holily, and disposing all in Your wisdom.

verses.text: But I who am more ready to go forward than backward, never continue in one stay, because changes sevenfold pass over me.
verses.modernizedText: But I who am more ready to go forward than backward, never continue in one state, because sevenfold changes pass over me.

verses.text: Yet it quickly becometh better when it so pleaseth Thee, and Thou puttest forth Thy hand to help me; because Thou alone canst aid without help of man, and canst so strengthen me that my countenance shall be no more changed, but my heart shall be turned to Thee, and rest in Thee alone.
verses.modernizedText: Yet it quickly becomes better when it so pleases You, and You put forth Your hand to help me; because You alone can aid without help of man, and can so strengthen me that my countenance will no more be changed, but my heart will be turned to You, and rest in You alone.

verses.text: Wherefore, if I but knew well how to reject all human consolations, whether for the sake of gaining devotion, or because of the necessity by which I was compelled to seek Thee, seeing there is no man who can comfort me; then could I worthily trust in Thy grace, and rejoice in the gift of new consolation.
verses.modernizedText: Therefore, if I only knew well how to reject all human consolations, whether for the sake of gaining devotion, or because of the necessity by which I was compelled to seek You, seeing there is no man who can comfort me; then I could worthily trust in Your grace, and rejoice in the gift of new consolation.

verses.text: Thanks be to Thee, from whom all cometh, whensoever it goeth well with me!
verses.modernizedText: Thanks be to You, from whom all comes, whenever it goes well with me!

verses.text: But I am vanity and nothing in Thy sight, a man inconstant and weak.
verses.modernizedText: But I am vanity and nothing in Your sight, a man inconstant and weak.

verses.text: What then have I whereof to glory, or why do I long to be held in honour?
verses.modernizedText: What then have I to glory in, or why do I long to be held in honor?

verses.text: Is it not for nought?
verses.modernizedText: Is it not for nothing?

verses.text: This also is utterly vain.
verses.modernizedText: This also is utterly vain.

verses.text: Verily vain glory is an evil plague, the greatest of vanities, because it draweth us away from the true glory, and robbeth us of heavenly grace.
verses.modernizedText: Truly vainglory is an evil plague, the greatest of vanities, because it draws us away from the true glory, and robs us of heavenly grace.

verses.text: For whilst a man pleaseth himself he displeaseth Thee; whilst he gapeth after the praises of man, he is deprived of true virtues.
verses.modernizedText: For while a man pleases himself he displeases You; while he reaches eagerly after the praises of man, he is deprived of true virtues.

verses.text: But true glory and holy rejoicing lieth in glorying in Thee and not in self; in rejoicing in Thy Name, not in our own virtue; in not taking delight in any creature, save only for Thy sake.
verses.modernizedText: But true glory and holy rejoicing lie in glorying in You and not in self; in rejoicing in Your Name, not in our own virtue; in not taking delight in any creature, except only for Your sake.

verses.text: Let thy Name, not mine be praised; let Thy work, not mine be magnified; let Thy holy Name be blessed, but to me let nought be given of the praises of men.
verses.modernizedText: Let Your Name, not mine, be praised; let Your work, not mine, be magnified; let Your holy Name be blessed, but to me let nothing be given of the praises of men.

verses.text: Thou art my glory, Thou art the joy of my heart.
verses.modernizedText: You are my glory, You are the joy of my heart.

verses.text: In Thee will I make my boast and be glad all the day long, but for myself let me not glory save only in my infirmities.(2)
verses.modernizedText: In You I will make my boast and be glad all the day long, but for myself let me not glory except only in my infirmities.(2)

verses.text: Let the Jews seek the honour which cometh from one another; but I will ask for that which cometh from God only.(3) Truly all human glory, all temporal honour, all worldly exultation, compared to Thy eternal glory, is but vanity and folly.
verses.modernizedText: Let the Jews seek the honor which comes from one another; but I will ask for that which comes from God only.(3) Truly all human glory, all temporal honor, all worldly exultation, compared to Your eternal glory, is but vanity and folly.

verses.text: O God my Truth and my Mercy, Blessed Trinity, to Thee alone be all praise, honour, power, and glory for ever and for ever.
verses.modernizedText: O God my Truth and my Mercy, Blessed Trinity, to You alone be all praise, honor, power, and glory forever and forever.

verses.text: Amen.
verses.modernizedText: Amen.
